chunks: Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Mughayrah informed us, saying: Mansur ibn Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili narrated from Abd Allah ibn Mikkan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about recognition (al-ma'rifa), is it acquired? He said: No. It was asked of him: Then is it from the making of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, and from His gift? He said: Yes, and the servants do not have a part in it, but they have the acquisition of actions. And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the actions of the servants are created with a created decree, not with constitutional creation. And the meaning of that is that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has always been Knowing of their measures before their existence.

key_terms.خَلْقَ تَقْدِيرٍ: Created decree (actions created by God's knowledge/decree)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between acquired recognition and divine gift in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the theological tension between divine grace and human agency by distinguishing 'recognition' (al-ma'rifa) as a pure divine gift from 'actions,' which are acquired through human effort. He clarifies that human actions are created via 'created decree' (khalq taqdir) rather than 'constitutional creation' (khalq takwin), emphasizing that God’s eternal knowledge of these actions precedes their actual existence, a nuance central to Shia discussions on predestination and free will.
